title: Rewrite exporter stream and introduce adaptive sampling core
creator: Marco Rios
description: We are seeing repeated OOMs and long tail latency in the observability hotpath under bursty workloads. Root cause analysis points to high allocations in the exporter path (buffering full batches in memory per-tenant) and a one-size-fits-all sampling configuration that floods downstream exporters during traffic spikes. This ticket rewrites the exporter from a buffered batch model to a streaming, backpressure-aware exporter and introduces an adaptive sampling core that adjusts sampling decisions based on dynamic trace signals and export queue depth.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end ingestion: traces/metrics/logs can be exported using new stream exporter with <10% CPU increase vs baseline under steady load
Memory usage: pod peak RSS for observability agent reduced by >=40% during 10k rps burst replay in test harness
Tail latency: 95th percentile export latency reduced by at least 30% during burst tests
No data loss: high-priority traces (span tagged 'error' or 'user-transaction') preserved at >99% under load via adaptive sampling override
Compatibility: exporter supports both OTLP/gRPC and our legacy envelope protocol, feature-flagged and toggleable
E2E tests and a load playbook added to the repo and CI (see linked_prs)
technical_notes: Design summary: (1) Replace large per-tenant batch queues with a streaming encoder that writes directly to a per-export connection using a bounded ring buffer and backpressure hooks. (2) Introduce a small central adaptive sampler module that consumes trace metadata and export-queue metrics to emit sampling decisions; decisions are cached per-trace-id for KV cache reuse. (3) Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK from 1.13.x to 1.16.x to pick up non-blocking exporter improvements; keep shim layer for legacy import paths. Trade-offs: streaming reduces peak memory but can increase syscall rate; mitigated via coalesced write buffers and recycler pools. We intentionally avoid introducing a new sidecar to keep deployment surface area small for Dedicated and Private customers.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed — prototype streaming writer that sends OTLP partial batches landed in spike branch. Memory profile shows 55% peak reduction in micro-bench.
2026-03-04: Chosen ringbuf implementation and tuned capacity; decided on 64KB coalescing window to balance latency and syscalls.
2026-03-06: Adaptive sampler design doc reviewed by Research/Applied ML; agreed on two heuristics: error-prioritize and queue-depth-throttle.
2026-03-09: Started main PR to rewrite exporter; initial end-to-end smoke passing in local integration harness.
2026-03-12: Integration test flagged a regression with legacy envelope serializer — compatibility shim added and test updated.
review_feedback: Infra review (Lina Chen): prefer bounded-tokens semaphore rather than global mutex for backpressure to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Security (Rajiv Malhotra): ensure exporter uses mTLS credentials rotation; added checklist to rollout_plan.
Performance (Jasmine Ortega): recommend object pool for span-serialization to reduce GC pressure; implemented in serializer v2.
testing_notes: Synthetic load harness updated to run multi-tenant burst tests (10 tenants, 10k rps for 60s). CI now runs a lightweight smoke of streaming exporter; full stress tests run nightly on dedicated perf runners. Use metric 'obs.exporter.queue_depth' and 'obs.exporter.memory_rss' dashboards when validating.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind 'stream_exporter' and 'adaptive_sampler'. 2) Canary on 5% of traffic for 24h in hosted; monitor queue_depth, export_errors, and host RSS. 3) Gradual rollout by doubling canary every 12h with manual pause if export_errors > 0.1% or queue_depth spikes unexpectedly. 4) For Dedicated/Private, ship as opt-in upgrade with migration guide and toggle.
notes: Follow-ups: (A) Evaluate converting high-cardinality metric labels to stable hash + label mapping to further cut memory; separate ticket after this lands. (B) Consider exposing sampler heuristics to Console as low-level knobs for enterprise customers.
